earlier_scan.source_named: ISO 639-3 code mhh retired 2014 (change request 2013-011); only survey mentions of this extinct pidgin, no linguistic description at all.

sources.note: Nothing; states 'Two spurious languages have been claimed in the literature: Emok and Maskoy Pidgin' without citation.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2013. Change Request Number 2013-011 (submitted by Hannes Kalisch, Nengvaanemkeskama Nempayvaam Enlhet; supported by Alain Fabre): retire [mhh] Maskoy Pidgin as non-existent; adopted 2014-02-03. Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; no linguistic data at all. §3(c), p. 2: 'There is no evidence to show that this language has ever existed.. no type of pidgin has developed. Either a dominant language has been used by all, or members of each group have used their own language and the others have developed the ability to understand it (a passive bi- or multilingualism).. today no Enlhet-Enenlhet language is spoken in the Puerto La Victoria region; ethnic groups belonging to the Enlhet-Enenlhet speak an adapted version of Paraguayan Guarani.' Sources cited: Unruh & Kalisch 2003 (Thule 14/15) and Fabre 2005/2…

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2013. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 17th ed., entry 'Maskoy Pidgin' [mhh] (web edition, the Internet Archive capture 2013).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. The only characterisation of the variety anywhere: 'Population: No known L1 speakers. Location: Puerto Victoria. Language Status 9 (Second language only). Classification: Pidgin, Mascoian based. Language Use: A mixed language formerly used in a tannin factory with Lengua [leg], Sanapaná [sap], Angaite (dialect of) [sap], Guana [gva], and Toba-Maskoy [tmf] influences. Speakers may have returned to former areas and languages, or to Guaraní-speaking rural areas. Other Comments: Different from Toba-Maskoy [tmf]. Probably no remaining speakers.'

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005 [online revision 2021-03-12]. Los pueblos del Gran Chaco y sus lenguas, primera parte: Los enlhet-enenlhet del Chaco Paraguayo. Suplemento Antropológico (Asunción) 40(1): 503-569; revised online version 76 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (ethnolinguistic survey + bibliography, no phonology). Does not mention a 'Maskoy Pidgin' or mhh at all; pp. 15-17 report that the groups who now self-designate as 'maskoy' around Puerto Casado/La Victoria speak a variety of Paraguayan Guaraní as first language (2002 census: 722 of 756 'maskoy' speak Guaraní at home) and uses 'pidgin' only as a generic label for a stage of language shift; notes (Kalisch p.c.) that this Maskoy Guaraní may differ from standard Paraguayan Guaraní and 'merecería un estudio aparte'.

sources.citation: Gordon, Raymond G., Jr. (ed.). 2005. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 15th ed., entry 'Maskoy Pidgin' [mhh] (web edition, Internet Archive copy 2005 and 2009).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Population: No estimate available. Region: Puerto Victoria. Classification: Pidgin, Mascoian based. Language use: A mixed language formerly used in a tannin factory with Lengua, Sanapana, Angaite, Guana, and Toba-Maskoy influences. Speakers are reported to have returned to former areas and languages, or to Guaraní-speaking rural areas. Speakers also use Paraguayan Guaraní. Comments: Different from Toba-Maskoy. Second language only.' No source given.
Nothing; the page lists only the ISO change request 2013-011 as its sole reference and repeats that the code was retired as non-existent.

sources.citation: Joshua Project, people-group profile 13574/PA 'Maskoy Pidgin in Paraguay'.
sources.note: Nothing linguistic; lists the group's language as Paraguayan Guarani [gug]; cites only a Refworld/Minority Rights document and Samaritan's Purse.

sources.citation: Kalisch, Hannes. 2004. 'Hablar y hacerse hablar: el guaraní de los maskoy' / Kalisch's work on the Guaraní variety spoken by the Puerto Casado 'maskoy' (referred to by Fabre 2005: 16 as Kalisch c.p. and Kalisch 2004b).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: If anything linguistic is ever written about the speech of the ex-tannin-factory community it will be a description of their variety of Paraguayan Guaraní, not a Mascoian pidgin; stress there would follow Guaraní (final/oxytone default). Only relevant if the catalog wants to record what actually replaced the supposed pidgin.

sources.citation: Unruh, Ernesto & Hannes Kalisch. 2003. Enlhet-Enenlhet. Una familia lingüística chaqueña. Thule, Rivista italiana di studi americanistici 14/15: 207-231.

sources.note: The one published source the change request cites for the sociolinguistic situation of the Puerto La Victoria 'maskoy'; would confirm at first hand that no pidgin existed. It is a family overview, not a description of any pidgin, and would not yield a stress statement.
